# Porcelain

> A diff does not tell you what changed. The agent that wrote it can. In Porcelain, it walks you through each decision, and you comment back before you keep the change.

Agents write the code. Porcelain is where you read it. It sits beside your agent and does not replace it: the agent publishes a walkthrough to Porcelain over MCP, you read it, reply on the code, and the agent reads your reply where it is working. It works with any agent that speaks MCP.

Porcelain runs on the machine that holds your repositories. The Mac app runs on Apple silicon; the server runs on Linux or Mac and starts with `npx @fabiofiorita/porcelain@latest serve`. You review in a browser, the Mac app, and soon an iPhone and iPad app. The server, the apps and the MCP tools are open source under the MIT license.

## Pages

- [Porcelain](https://porcelain.fabiofiorita.com/): The walkthrough, comments on the code, proof, files, history and remote environments.
- [Install](https://porcelain.fabiofiorita.com/install): The Mac app, or a server on Linux or Mac, on the machine that holds your repositories.
- [Privacy](https://porcelain.fabiofiorita.com/privacy): Porcelain has no account, no analytics, and no copy of your code. Here is everything it knows about you, and the source to prove it.

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/FabioFiorita/porcelain): The server, the apps, the updater and this site, under the MIT license.
